episodes.title: OpenAI’s Noam Brown: Why Game Theory Didn’t Lead to General Intelligence (Live at No Limit Finals)
episodes.description: Noam Brown built the first AIs to beat top poker professionals, then concluded that game theory, the field his career was built on, was not the path to general intelligence. Recorded live at the Finals of No Limit, Sequoia’s pokerbot tournament, the OpenAI researcher describes his “crisis of faith”: game theory assumes everyone is rational, and the Diplomacy bots that won were the ones trained on human data to model how people actually behave in the messy real world. That sent him to OpenAI and the work that became o1, at a time when much of the field believed a bigger pre-trained model would solve everything. episodes.title: REPLAY: The Story of Apple Pay | Jennifer Bailey (2024)
episodes.description: When Apple Pay launched in the U.S., only about 3% of merchants accepted contactless payments. A decade later, Jennifer Bailey has helped expand it to 75 markets and more than 11,000 bank and network partners. Jennifer joins a16z General Partner Alex Rampell to tell the story of building Apple Pay, from solving the chicken-and-egg problem of banks, merchants, and consumers to designing payments around security and privacy without Apple seeing individual transactions. They also discuss the expansion from payments into transit, tickets, car and hotel keys, and digital IDs, plus why customer experience, patience, and timing have shaped Jennifer’s approach to building new products inside Apple. episodes.title: Nvidia, China, and the open-model race: Reflection AI's Misha Laskin on a $25B bet
episodes.description: Reflection AI has quickly become the West’s best hope to rival China on open-source AI. Co-founder and CEO Misha Laskin, formerly of Google DeepMind, joins Rapid Response shortly after the release of Beam, Reflection's first open-weight model, to explain why he sees open models as a way to own intelligence rather than rent it. He makes the national security case for American models that win on merit, and he says open models have gone from a minority to a majority of AI token share in just six months. He also shares how Reflection plans to make money when its weights are free, and where Nvidia chips fit into the race with China. episodes.description: On Monday morning, Nvidia's board stunned the world and announced that it was reinstating Jensen Huang as CEO. Reportedly, President Trump pressed the board to bring back Huang, and his return kicked off a historic rally for the chip maker. (Nasdaq 100 futures went up so fast yesterday, they briefly halted trading.) episodes.title: 現場作業を学ぶAIと5億円の企業価値担保融資とは？
episodes.description: 今回のエピソードでは、テクノロジー企業の最新資金調達動向から注目の2つのトピックを解説します。 前半は、シリーズAで4,700万米ドルを調達したHumyn Labsを取り上げます。同社はウェブ上の知識ではなく、工場や農場などの現場作業を記録し、熟練者の経験をロボット学習用のデータセットへ変換するフィジカルAI基盤を展開しています。 後半は、新設された企業価値担保権を用いた国内の先駆的融資事例です。設立2年目のマイクロニティが、不動産担保や個人保証に頼らず、買収先であるIBT総合研究所の事業価値やキャッシュフローを評価され、静岡銀行から5億円の買収資金を調達しました。 現場作業から暗黙知を学ぶロボティクスAIと、事業そのものを評価して成長資金を供給する新たな融資慣行。技術と金融の双方が迎える変革の現在地をお届けします。
